runners.name: Never Enough
runners.spotlight: By No Nay Never out of 5f/5.7f winner (including 2yo/Listed; RPR 108); 15-2 when second of 11 for novice at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 26 days ago, running on from midfield; that form has taken some knocks but still makes appeal in this line-up and this Group 2 Gimcrack entry showed plenty of promise.
runners.comment: 15-2 when running-on second of 11 at Windsor (6f, good to firm); Group 2 Gimcrack entry

runners.name: Perfect Strike
runners.spotlight: 75,000euros yearling, 280,000euros breeze-up 2yo by Perfect Power; third foal; dam unplaced at 7.5f-10.5f in France, sister to US 1m Grade 2 winner Tamahere, half-sister to 10.5f Listed winner Shadan; leading yard has not yet found its stride with 2yos this term but he still needs a check.
runners.comment: 280,000euros breeze-up 2yo by Perfect Power; from a leading yard and needs a check

runners.name: Izuba
runners.spotlight: 135,000gns yearling by Siyouni; third foal; half-brother to 10.6f AW winner Seola (RPR 70); dam French 7.5f 2yo/10.5f Listed winner, closely related to useful French 7f winner Markhor, out of 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Vorda; from a leading stable, so needs a close look.
runners.comment: 135,000gns yearling by Siyouni; from a leading stable, so needs a close look

runners.name: Tumishi
runners.spotlight: 180,000gns breeze-up 2yo by Havana Grey; 11-1 when beaten a shade over 3l in a novice at Nottingham (6f, good) early last month, coming from towards rear for fourth of 12; non-runner twice since; looks sure to improve and has major each-way claims for in-form stable.
runners.comment: 4th of 12 at Nottingham (6f, good) early in June; major each-way claims for in-form stable

runners.name: Astralite
runners.spotlight: 55,000gns yearling by Dark Angel; second foal; dam US 5f-8.5f turf winner, out of graded-placed US 1m winner; gelded and others look more striking on paper, even though stable was off the mark with this year's 2yos this month.
runners.comment: 55,000gns yearling by Dark Angel; second foal; dam US 5f-8.5f turf winner; gelded

runners.name: Crazee In Havana
runners.spotlight: Seventh foal; Havana Grey half-brother to winners Mister Winston (7.6f-8.5f; RPR 106), Kinks (5f-7f including 2yo/Bahrain; 96) and Crazee Icon (7.6f; 84); dam 6f AW winner (70), closely related to Listed-placed 5f winner Thesme; late foal but with in-form trainer who won this race in 2022 and 2023, both with something second time out.
runners.comment: Havana Grey half-brother to winners including Mister Winston (RPR 106) and Kinks (96)

runners.name: Silent Sadhu
runners.spotlight: 3,000gns yearling by Sergei Prokofiev; ran a great deal better than 150-1 suggested he would in a novice at Newbury (6f, good to firm) 16 days ago, getting hampered at the start but running on into sixth of 18, beaten just over 2l; it's not the best form in this field but was a promising debut.
runners.comment: 150-1 at Newbury (6f, good to firm) recently but ran on for 6th of 18, beaten just over 2l

runners.name: Public Affection
runners.spotlight: 110,000euros yearling by Showcasing; 10-1 when sixth of 13 in maiden at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 33 days ago, making some of the running; showed ability but big improvement is needed.
runners.comment: 10-1 when sixth of 13 at Windsor (6f, good to firm; led part of way); improvement needed

runners.name: Ahoy
runners.spotlight: 260,000gns breeze-up 2yo by Naval Crown; no show, however, when 25-1 for maiden at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month, behind Public Affection.
runners.comment: 260,000gns breeze-up 2yo; no show, however, when 25-1 at Windsor (6f, good to firm)

runners.name: Velozee
runners.spotlight: Made it 2-2 with easy win in four-runner Listed race at the Curragh (5f, good) in May; faded in Group 3 at Naas (6f, good) next time but kept on well when eighth of 27 in the Group 2 Queen Mary here (5f, good to firm) at the Royal meeting, where she didn't enjoy an ideal passage; closely matched with Alta Regina on that latest form and the return to 6f is worth a go; chance.
runners.comment: Kept on for eighth in the 5f Queen Mary here; the return to 6f is worth a go; chance
runners.owner: Gary Matthews, Steve Weston & Lucky Hat

runners.name: Moonrise
runners.spotlight: Made all at 5-1 in small-field novice at Kempton (6f, AW) on debut then went close at 66-1 in the Listed Windsor Castle Stakes here (6f, good to firm) at the Royal meeting, racing prominently throughout; on the shortlist.
runners.comment: 66-1 runner-up in the Listed Windsor Castle over C&D and she's on the shortlist

runners.name: Dark Issue
runners.spotlight: Impressive on debut at Goodwood (6f, good) in May and confirmed that promise when fourth of 25 in the Group 3 Albany Stakes over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm); she has to be firmly in calculations.
runners.comment: Impressive on debut at Goodwood then fourth in the Albany over C&D; firmly in calculations

runners.name: Dee's Funny Girl
runners.spotlight: 16-1 winner for Michael Keady on debut at Thirsk (5f, good) in May, despite being denied a clear run, and then sixth of 25 at 80-1 in the Group 3 Albany over C&D (good to firm); she has just over 3l to find with Dark Issue (who was fourth) on that Royal Ascot form but could have more to offer; sold for £150,000 just before the Royal meeting; respected on stable debut.
runners.comment: Thirsk win on debut then sixth in the Albany here; could have more to offer; stable debut

runners.name: Glorious Game
runners.spotlight: Made all on debut at Windsor (6f, good to soft) last month then dead-heated for first in a Listed race at Newmarket (6f, good to firm), where she was the 7-4 favourite; open to further improvement and represents last year's winning yard; she's one to consider.
runners.comment: Made it 2-2 with Listed dead-heat at Newmarket; represents last year's winning yard

runners.name: Alta Regina
runners.spotlight: 240,000gns breeze-up buy who won easily on debut at Lingfield (5f, good to firm) in May and kept on well for sixth of 27 in the Group 2 Queen Mary here at the Royal meeting (5f, good to firm); the step up to 6f could be a positive move and she's a leading contender.
runners.comment: Kept on for sixth in the 5f Queen Mary here and could improve for 6f; leading contender

runners.name: The Can Can Queen
runners.spotlight: Won at Ripon (6f, good) in May on second start and suited by the return to 6f when close Listed third at Newmarket last month (good to firm; led; behind Glorious Game); stable won this in 2017 and 2023 but she needs another step forward if she's to come out on top today.
runners.comment: Close Listed third at Newmarket last month but needs another step forward today

runners.name: Harlequin Sky
runners.spotlight: Improved upon her first two runs when 1l third of 25 at 125-1 in the Listed Windsor Castle Stakes over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm; Moonrise second); can be in the mix if backing up that performance.
runners.comment: Improved upon first 2 runs when 125-1 third in Windsor Castle; in the mix if backing it up

runners.name: Magnesium
runners.spotlight: Won modest novice race at Kempton (6f, AW) in May on second run, then well beaten at 300-1 in the Albany over C&D (good to firm); hard to fancy.
runners.comment: Won modest AW novice on second start then well beaten at 300-1 in the Albany here

runners.name: Miss Kodi
runners.spotlight: 95,000euros yearling; first foal; dam unraced half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 1 winner Arcano; 6-1, won by 7l in six-runner novice on last month's debut at Chepstow (6f, good to soft); this is a vastly tougher race but she's clearly a bright prospect; remains to be seen where her limitations lie.
runners.comment: 7l win on debut at Chepstow and it remains to be seen where her limitations lie

runners.name: Nuit d'Eclair
runners.spotlight: 280,000gns yearling who won at 12-1 on this month's debut at Newbury (6f, good to firm); others have more substance to their form but she's a likeable prospect who has plenty of scope to progress.
runners.comment: Won on this month's debut at Newbury and she has plenty of scope to progress

runners.name: Touleen
runners.spotlight: Edged out by Sukanya in the Fred Darling at Newbury on reappearance but had that reopposing rival behind her when an improved second to Precise in the Group 1 Coronation over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting; even better than the result (met trouble a few times) on that occasion and a similar level of performance will make her hard to beat back in a Group 3.
runners.comment: Shaped well when second in Group 1 over C&D latest; hard to beat at this lower level

runners.name: Kon Tiki
runners.spotlight: Missed the rest of the season after finishing seventh in the Coronation over C&D at 2025 Royal Ascot but has returned with two fine runs behind Blue Bolt, latterly when fourth of 15 in the Duke Of Cambridge over C&D (good to firm); the one likely to give Touleen most to do.
runners.comment: Good fourth of 15 in C&D Group 2 at Royal meeting and the main threat to Touleen

runners.name: Sukanya
runners.spotlight: Improved upon her 2yo form when coming from the back of the pack to beat Touleen and win the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good) on her reappearance; bounced back from a tame effort in the Irish 1,000 Guineas at the Curragh when sixth of nine to Precise in the Coronation over C&D last month but Touleen was 2.5l ahead of her in second on that occasion.
runners.comment: Beat Touleen to win Fred Darling but behind same rival in Coronation over C&D latest

runners.name: Esna
runners.spotlight: Stepped up on reappearance form when winning Listed event over 1m2f at Newbury (good) in May; can probably be forgiven her subsequent effort in the Prix de Diane at Chantilly after pressing the pace out wide; drops back to 1m now; even a return to her best probably won't be enough, though.
runners.comment: 1m2f Listed win in May; probably best forgiven poor run in French Group 1 since

runners.name: Skydance
runners.spotlight: Highly tried last season, showing pretty smart form when second in Leopardstown Group 3 and when beaten under 4l in Group 1 Moyglare at the Curragh; dropped to maiden company to edge out subsequent Oaks winner Thundering On on 1m Leopardstown reappearance; off since but evidently capable when fresh and likely to have a say if handling the quicker ground (raced on good or softer so far).
runners.comment: Held own at Group level at 2 and edged out Thundering On in maiden on return; off since

runners.name: Arisaig
runners.spotlight: Losing run up to 16; has run some fine races in that period but her hold-up style dictates that things need to drop right and she got going too late when third in 1m Pontefract Listed race 18 days ago; prior to that she finished around 2l behind the reopposing Kon Tiki when eighth of 15 to Blue Bolt in the Duke Of Cambridge over C&D at the Royal meeting (good to firm).
runners.comment: Smart hold-up performer but needs things to drop right and her losing run is now up to 16

runners.name: Cheshire Dancer
runners.spotlight: Won this race on good ground 12 months ago but was on an upward curve at that stage and doesn't obviously arrive in anything like the same form this time round.
runners.comment: Winner of this last year but doesn't obviously arrive in the same form

runners.name: Pina Sonata
runners.spotlight: Came up well short in Group 1/Listed events in the second half of 2025 but different story on Kempton AW reappearance, readily seeing off ten rivals in 1m Listed race; something presumably not right when favourite for an Epsom Group 3 on Derby day (good to soft), finishing a distant last of seven; given seven weeks to get over that.
runners.comment: Ready AW Listed win (1m) on return; something not right when last in Epsom Group 3 since

runners.name: Extremely Zain
runners.spotlight: Novice wins on his first two starts and he made it 3-3 when winning a big-field handicap at York (7f, good) last month, doing it comfortably despite having to wait for a run; there is a strong suspicion he's a Group-race winner in the making and he could take an 8lb rise in his stride.
runners.comment: Made it 3-3 with impressive win at York and he could take an 8lb rise in his stride

runners.name: Amazing Journey
runners.spotlight: Won at Kempton (6f, AW) last month before near-miss at Epsom (6f, good), and back on the scoresheet with ready win here (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; under a 3lb penalty this progressive 3yo is 5lb ahead of the handicapper today, and he showed promise over 7f last season; major player.
runners.comment: Ready win over 6f here a fortnight ago and he's ahead of the handicapper under a penalty

runners.name: Stellar Sunrise
runners.spotlight: Reappeared with a convincing handicap win at Newbury (7f, good) in April; underwhelming favourite in Listed races at Newmarket and Epsom on next two starts but gelded since and returns to a handicap this afternoon, and he could have a part to play if rediscovering the Newbury form.
runners.comment: Convincing handicap win at Newbury in April; two lesser efforts followed, but gelded since

runners.name: Saytarr
runners.spotlight: Won early this year on first three runs for James Horton (7f/1m, AW) before good third here (1m, good to firm) and a fifth of seven at Sandown (1m, good); won at Kempton (1m, AW) next time; could give a good account but he's 6-9 on AW as opposed to 0-10 on turf, which tempers enthusiasm.
runners.comment: Ran well here in May but he's 6-9 on AW as opposed to 0-10 on turf

runners.name: Back In Black
runners.spotlight: Admirably consistent in defeat this term and he was a close second to Aalto in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) recently; races off the same mark today (due a 2lb rise) and could again be thereabouts.
runners.comment: Close second in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket; has the same mark and could be thereabouts

runners.name: Philanthropist
runners.spotlight: Won in first-time cheekpieces (retained since) at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) in April and has continued in good heart on his two outings since; however, he's up in grade this afternoon and needs something extra.
runners.comment: Won at Yarmouth in April and has continued in good heart, but he's up in grade

runners.name: Completely Random
runners.spotlight: Returned to form when dropped back in trip in first-time cheekpieces (retained) in the Wokingham here (6f, good to firm) last month, finishing fast under Ryan Moore for a head second; on that evidence the return to 7f could be a good move and he's one to consider.
runners.comment: Finished fast for close second in the 6f Wokingham here; one to consider back up to 7f

runners.name: Aalto
runners.spotlight: His career-best efforts have come in the last three runnings of the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket (7f, good/good to firm), winning it in 2024 and a fortnight ago with a near-miss in between; under a 3lb penalty there's still mileage in his mark but he's never finished better than ninth from four visits here.
runners.comment: Excels in the Bunbury Cup, which he won again a fortnight ago; hasn't really shone here

runners.name: Mezcala
runners.spotlight: Reappeared with a win in the Spring Mile at Doncaster (good to soft) before good third at Newbury (1m, good), and took another step forward to win the Buckingham Palace over C&D (good to firm) at Royal Ascot; this 4yo is clearly progressive and could play another leading role up 4lb for last time.
runners.comment: Lightly raced 4yo who won over C&D at the Royal meeting and is clearly progressive

runners.name: Sword
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent sort who is opposable on the majority of his form over the last 12 months and was only sixth at Newmarket last time; however, he's popped up with the odd big run, finishing third in this last year and filling the same position in a big field at York last month; not a forlorn hope each-way.
runners.comment: Opposable on majority of form but pops up with the odd big run; third in this last year

runners.name: Two Tribes
runners.spotlight: Won this last year (good) and followed up in the Stewards' Cup at Goodwood (6f, good to soft); after a very good start to this year at Meydan he hasn't hit the same heights since; his recent seventh in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket was a step back in the right direction but he needs another today.
runners.comment: Won this last year; step back in right direction at Newmarket recently but needs another

runners.name: Ata Rangi
runners.spotlight: Two wins last term (1m/7f, AW/good) and he added another on his reappearance at Haydock (7f, good) in May; again ran well when fourth of 15 at Newbury (7f, good to soft) latest but his form needs to go to a new level today.
runners.comment: Won at Haydock on return then good fourth at Newbury, but form needs to go to a new level

runners.name: Leadman
runners.spotlight: Denied a clear run when fifth at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) latest and he's a type who needs things to drop right; however, he got up on the line at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) two runs ago and may have an each-way shout.
runners.comment: Needs things to drop right but he won at Doncaster two runs ago and may have an e-w shout

runners.name: Great Acclaim
runners.spotlight: Merely mid-division behind Aalto in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket a fortnight ago but this C&D brings out the best in him, as evidenced by this season's close-up finishes in the Victoria Cup (good) and Buckingham Palace Stakes (good to firm); could be bang there now back at Ascot.
runners.comment: Mid-division in the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket but this C&D brings out the best in him

runners.name: Arctic Dawn
runners.spotlight: 5yo who produced a career-best performance with authoritative win at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month; following a 9lb rise he was well beaten over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting 12 days later, finishing fourth of six in the unfavoured far-side group, but he's not written off.
runners.comment: Authoritative win at Doncaster last month; well beaten at Royal Ascot but not written off

runners.name: Golden Mind
runners.spotlight: Below his best on his last two runs, most recently over C&D at the Royal meeting; has some good C&D form, however, such as when fourth in both this race last year and the Victoria Cup in May; not ruled out each-way.
runners.comment: Below best on last two runs (C&D latest) but has some good C&D form; not ruled out e-w

races.race_name: King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Group 1)

runners.name: Calandagan
runners.spotlight: His flop in the Coronation Cup at Epsom last month can be excused by the substantial rain and he showed he was none the worse when winning the Group 1 Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud (1m4f, good to firm) three weeks ago; had just a neck to spare last time but did well to come from the back of the pack off a stop-start gallop; he's a six-time winner at the top level, including of this race last year, and holds leading claims.
runners.comment: Got back on track at Saint-Cloud with a sixth win at the top level; leading claims

runners.name: Kalpana
runners.spotlight: She's won the last two runnings of the Group 1 British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes here in October and she was a 1l second of five to Calandagan in this race last year; short-headed in the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting and she might not be far away.
runners.comment: Two C&D Group 1 wins and second in this race last year; she might not be far away

runners.name: Benvenuto Cellini
runners.spotlight: Favourite in the rain-affected Derby at Epsom last month, when he finished tenth past the post but was deemed to be a non-runner having got his leg caught in the stalls; subsequently justified favouritism in the Irish Derby at the Curragh (1m4f, good); this is a tougher test of his credentials but he brings star potential and he's Ryan Moore's mount of the Ballydoyle four; he may well be up to the task.
runners.comment: Won the Irish Derby; tougher test today but star potential and may well be up to the task

runners.name: Masquerade Ball
runners.spotlight: Won the Grade 1 Tenno Sho (Autumn) at Tokyo (1m2f, good to firm) last November and narrowly lost out to Calandagan in a titanic tussle in the Grade 1 Japan Cup there (1m4f, good to firm) later that month; bumped into prolific Grade 1 winner Romantic Warrior when second in the Grade 1 QEII Cup at Sha Tin (1m2f, good to firm) in April on his sole run this year and this Japanese raider could have a big part to play in his rematch with Calandagan.
runners.comment: Narrowly lost out to Calandagan in the Japan Cup; could have a big part to play in rematch

runners.name: Minnie Hauk
runners.spotlight: 1m4f Group 1 wins last summer in the Oaks, Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks before head second in the 1m4f Arc at Longchamp; back on song when runner-up in the Group 1 Prince of Wales's Stakes here (1m2f, good to firm) last month and, although she was beaten 4l and Ryan Moore rides stablemate Benvenuto Cellini today, she was behind the brilliant Ombudsman and could build on that latest effort now she's back up to 1m4f.
runners.comment: Runner-up in the 1m2f Prince of Wales's Stakes here; could build on it back up to 1m4f
runners.owner: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor

runners.name: Lambourn
runners.spotlight: Last season's Derby and Irish Derby winner who reappeared with a win in the Group 2 Huxley Stakes at Chester in May; however, he hasn't come up to scratch on his three starts since and needs to turn things around; the cheekpieces worn on his four outings this season are left off.
runners.comment: 2025 Derby and Irish Derby winner; has not come up to scratch since Group 2 win on return
runners.owner: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith

runners.name: Goliath
runners.spotlight: Won this in 2024 (good to firm) at 25-1 and has won four Group races since, the latest the Group 2 Grand Prix de Chantilly (1m4f, good) this May; bang there in the final furlong of the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes over C&D (good to firm) at the Royal meeting only for Christophe Soumillon to lose his irons; he has an each-way chance.
runners.comment: Won this in 2024 at 25-1; bang there in C&D Hardwicke latest only for rider to lose irons
runners.owner: Resolute Bloodstock & Philip Baron Von Ullmann

runners.name: Action
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in the Group 1 Futurity Trophy at Doncaster (1m, heavy) last October and filled the same position in the Group 2 Dante at York (10.2f, good) in May; however, he's been well beaten in the Derby and Irish Derby on his last two starts, having made the running; hard to fancy.
runners.comment: Second in the Dante at York in May but well beaten in the Derby and Irish Derby since
runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier

runners.name: Wurttemberg
runners.spotlight: 6yo who produced a clear career best when beaten a nose at 206-1 in the Grade 1 Tenno Sho (Spring) at Kyoto (2m, good to firm) in May; however, on a formline through the winner he has something to find with Calandagan and compatriot Masquerade Ball.
runners.comment: 206-1 Grade 1 runner-up at Kyoto in May but formlines suggest he has something to find

runners.name: Edwin Hubble
runners.spotlight: Two seconds and two thirds from his six starts; upped to 1m2f then 11.4f in handicaps for his two starts this season, best form in a never-nearer second of five last time; back up 2lb but could have more to give at this trip.
runners.comment: Best form in a never-nearer second of five last time (11.4f); could have more to give

runners.name: Masterinthewoods
runners.spotlight: Second of five last term in his only race on good to firm; won at Salisbury in May and improved again when a close second at Goodwood (again 1m4f on good) in June; the Goodwood winner scored again next time but this 4yo has been raised just 1lb and is heading the right way; big shout.
runners.comment: Close second at Goodwood (1m4f, good) latest start and the winner scored again next time

runners.name: Hengest
runners.spotlight: Won at Windsor, Lingfield (11.6f) and Yarmouth in May/June in his first three handicaps, before tailed off on rain-hit ground at Epsom and well beaten with cheekpieces added at York; no headgear today; not proven over quite this far and may have to resume improvement.
runners.comment: Well beaten in cheekpieces latest; not proven over this far; may have to resume progress
runners.owner: Gee Gees Racing, P Gleeson & N Barnes

runners.name: Mudita
runners.spotlight: Won maiden at Ripon (1m2f, good) in April; contested three small-field handicaps since, finishing third on last two occasions (1m4f/1m6f); while a return to 1m4f may help, she needs to raise her game.
runners.comment: Third in two small-field handicaps (1m4f/1m6f) and needs to raise her game

runners.name: Akho Mezzna
runners.spotlight: Wore cheekpieces last three outings, for a rallying second at Sandown (1m2f, good/good to firm) on last two occasions; better is needed but he shapes as if new trip is well worth a go.
runners.comment: Rallying second at Sandown (1m2f) on last two starts, shaping as if new trip is worth a go

runners.name: Patrol
runners.spotlight: Last won when sharing the spoils at Southwell (1m4f, AW) in April 2025; close second of 15 at Newbury (1m4f, good) in May was his best show this season and he acts on good to firm, but others are preferred for win purposes; this is a very rare run in headgear.
runners.comment: Close three runs ago; others are preferred for win purposes; a very rare run in headgear

runners.name: Oasis Sunrise
runners.spotlight: Turf wins this term at Bath (1m), Chepstow (1m4f) and Leicester (1m2f), with one of those under Ashley Lewis; however, her form has dropped off somewhat in 1m4f races on last two outings and this race demands more.
runners.comment: Three turf wins this term; form has dropped off somewhat in 1m4f races on last two outings

runners.name: Primo Lara
runners.spotlight: Won twice in 2024 for Jane Chapple-Hyam; spent a year with Jack Morland and got off the mark for him at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) 19 days ago; sold again for 22,000gns one day later and this is his first run back with his former yard; back up 4lb and not proven beyond an extended 1m2f (unraced over this far); tongue-tie and headgear worn for his last yard is removed; quite a few questions, but peak 2024 form was a bit better.
runners.comment: Won 19 days ago (9.4f, AW); 22,000gns sale one day later and he's back with former yard

runners.name: Ohara
runners.spotlight: 2yo win was over 1m on soft at a stiff track and he was stepped up to 1m4f when second of four at Chepstow (good to firm) on latest outing, his best show this term; needs to build on that but he saw the trip out very well and could have more in the tank.
runners.comment: Needs to build on it but he saw 1m4f out very well last time; could have more in the tank

runners.name: Taritino
runners.spotlight: Has won six races on the Flat at up to 1m6f and this year is going particularly well, with two hurdle wins and now two over about 1m4f on Flat (on good ground at Salisbury and Chester); raised 4lb to career-high mark but should be fine back on good to firm and he's never been better.
runners.comment: 1m4f wins on last two starts; raised 4lb to career-high mark but he's never been better

runners.name: A Daughters Love
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish; has done much better for new yard, including wins (1m2f, good to firm) under Jack Doughty at Chepstow and Leicester before her creditable fifth of ten at Wolverhampton (upped to 1m4f, AW); position 9lb out of the handicap this time, however, demands a leap forward.
runners.comment: Ran creditably at 1m4f latest but position 9lb out of the handicap demands a leap forward

runners.name: Sir Griflet
runners.spotlight: 1m6f and/or soft ground may excuse his latest start, when he raced freely in the lead in first-time cheekpieces; previously showed some ability over about 1m4f but more is needed, particularly as he is 5lb out of the handicap; tongue-tie is added and 7lb claimer is also recruited.
runners.comment: More is needed from him, particularly as he is 5lb out of the handicap; tongue-tie today

runners.name: Green Falcon
runners.spotlight: Below form sole start on good to firm; made the frame on all his four runs as 2yo, short-headed in a 1m1f maiden on final outing; cheekpieces were added for handicap/seasonal debut at Kempton (1m3f, AW) and he wasn't beaten far but hung right and came last of five; off 115 days since (gelded) and needs overall improvement.
runners.comment: Last of five on handicap/seasonal debut (1m3f, AW); off 115 days since (gelded)

runners.name: Tailorman
runners.spotlight: Acts on good to firm; in good form over 1m6f/2m last June, including for a Chester win off 3lb lower than today; well held on sole start here (last July) and not seen since last September; he ran well first time out last season but others look more persuasive today.
runners.comment: In good form over 1m6f/2m last June, including for a Chester win off 3lb lower than today

runners.name: Bint Al Daar
runners.spotlight: 2-21 on turf and 3-21 on AW, with latest win in March; usually seen over shorter; her last turf run was last September and that 2025 turf campaign went the wrong way, but at least she has a lower mark this time.
runners.comment: 2-21 on turf and 3-21 on AW, latest win in March; 2025 turf campaign went the wrong way

runners.name: Grizedale
runners.spotlight: Won at Kempton (1m, AW) on second run since being gelded and he followed up in fine style at Newbury (1m, good to firm); up 9lb since last time but this progressive 4yo could still play a leading role.
runners.comment: Progressive 4yo who has won his last two, in fine style at Newbury most recently; up 9lb

runners.name: Spanish Voice
runners.spotlight: Two wins on the two Newmarket courses this season (1m, good to firm/good), the latest coming last month when held up; only fifth to Asmen Warrior at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) 16 days ago but saw plenty of daylight in a prominent position and may not have been seen to best effect; this lightly raced 4yo remains one to be interested in.
runners.comment: Two wins this season; only fifth last time but may not have been seen to best effect

runners.name: Frankies Dream
runners.spotlight: Twice close up in big-field handicaps at York (1m1f/1m, good) last month before fading when upped to 10.2f there (good to firm) a fortnight ago, when he failed to settle; could be a contender back down in trip.
runners.comment: In good form over 1m1f/1m at York before fading over 10.2f there a fortnight ago

runners.name: Asmen Warrior
runners.spotlight: With this visor back on, and back on better ground, he returned to form with a well-backed win at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) a fortnight ago, coming clear with a runner-up who was returning from a long absence and won at Sandown on Thursday; an 8lb rise might not stop him.
runners.comment: Won in good style at Newmarket recently and form franked; an 8lb rise might not stop him

runners.name: Spoken Truth
runners.spotlight: 0-13 since winning in April 2024 on his second start and the drop back to 1m poses a question; only sixth of nine at Sandown three weeks ago but running well previously; might have an each-way chance if bouncing back.
runners.comment: 0-13 since winning in April 2024 on his second start but some good runs this season

runners.name: Urban Lion
runners.spotlight: Good fifth over C&D in last season's Royal Hunt Cup (good to firm) and he reappeared with a win in the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) in March; however, well beaten on both starts since; has to get back on track.
runners.comment: Effective over C&D and won the Lincoln on reappearance but well beaten on both runs since

runners.name: Blue Rc
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who has been runner-up in competitive handicaps on three of his four starts since April, most recently in last month's 28-runner Royal Hunt Cup over C&D (good to firm); climbing the weights in defeat but he's nevertheless firmly in calculations.
runners.comment: Runner-up on three of his four starts since April, most recently in the C&D Royal Hunt Cup

runners.name: Christian David
runners.spotlight: Mixed form this season but kept on well for close fourth at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last Saturday; might not be far away back up to 1m.
runners.comment: Kept on well for close fourth over 7f at Doncaster last Saturday; might not be far away

runners.name: Crown Board
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent but he's just 1lb higher than when making all at Chelmsford (1m, AW) last December and he returned from a break with an encouraging third at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago, when again making the running; might not face much opposition for the lead; chance.
runners.comment: Inconsistent but returned from break with encouraging third at Newmarket; chance

runners.name: Salam Dubawi
runners.spotlight: Won at Hamilton (1m1f, good) in May on second start for yard and third past the post in the competitive John Smith's Cup at York on July 11 (10.2f, good to firm; demoted to fifth due to interference); only fourth of five at Hamilton (8.3f, good to firm) five days later but set a steady pace, which may not have suited; not ruled out each-way.
runners.comment: Third past the post in the John Smith's Cup at York; had an excuse next time

runners.name: Hickory
runners.spotlight: 8yo who hasn't been at the top of his game this season (twice here); however, he took a step back in the right direction when sixth of 13 to Asmen Warrior at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last time and he may be able to build on it back at a track where he had a good record last season.
runners.comment: Step back in right direction at Newmarket last time and he has a good record here

runners.name: Emperor Spirit
runners.spotlight: Ran a stormer over C&D on his seasonal return; the ground went against him at Epsom on Derby day and he has quickly bounced back with placed efforts at Beverley and Newmarket; up 2lb for latest near-miss but still on a good mark; Oisin Murphy booked; decent chance.
runners.comment: Conditions no problem and arrives in top form; Oisin Murphy booked; one to take seriously

runners.name: Bassenthwaite
runners.spotlight: Won two of his five starts as a 2yo, including a wide-margin nursery success at Wolverhampton in November; he hasn't seen his race out in two handicap runs this year (5f/6f) but he should be sharper for last month's return from a break, he represents a yard that excels with this type and he has few miles on the clock; revival not out of the question.
runners.comment: 2-5 as a 2yo; not fired yet in 2026 but down in the weights and still has low mileage

runners.name: Getreadytorumble
runners.spotlight: Hugely progressive as a 3yo, winning three times; highly tried this year and he has run with credit in defeat, notably his Listed third at Naas in April; 9lb higher than for his last handicap run (a 5f win at Doncaster) and could prove vulnerable.
runners.comment: Progressive in 2025; highly tried this year & come up just shy; tough task off top weight

runners.name: Indian Run
runners.spotlight: Stays 6f well but he isn't short of speed and this belated first attempt at 5f looks an interesting move; arrives in top form, successful at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) 24 days ago, and a 4lb rise still leaves him with handicapping potential.
runners.comment: Arrives in good form and a 4lb rise for latest Thirsk win is fair enough; first 5f start

runners.name: All Ways Glamorous
runners.spotlight: Two C&D runs have seen him make the frame in big-field events; easily saw off four rivals in a handicap at Ffos Las (5f, good) 26 days ago; the combination of a 7lb rise and considerably more demanding opposition could scupper a follow up.
runners.comment: Conditions fine and he's on the up but this is much tougher than the race he won last time

runners.name: Bolo Neighs
runners.spotlight: Kept on well when winning a 6f handicap (good) here in May; not so good on his next two starts but he ran well for third back here (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; drops back to 5f with cheekpieces enlisted; others preferred for the win.
runners.comment: Two best efforts in 2026 have come at Ascot but at 6f; drops to 5f with cheekpieces added

runners.name: Rocking Ends
runners.spotlight: His two Ascot defeats came at the Royal meeting when a big outsider; arrives on the back of an easy win at Newmarket (5f, good to firm; visor reinstated) but a 6lb rise for that could leave him vulnerable.
runners.comment: Easy Newmarket win eight days ago; 6lb rise in a hotter race demands more of him

runners.name: King Of Light
runners.spotlight: Powered clear of his rivals in a 6f handicap at Windsor last month; reared at the start and missed the break over C&D a fortnight ago; perhaps a shade high in the weights for now.
runners.comment: Impressed over 6f at Windsor in June; blew start over C&D latest; needs a personal best

runners.name: Sir Yoshi
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish 4yo; slow start to life with this stable but he has dropped in the weights and his last two runs have been more encouraging, notably his Pontefract third eight days ago; should go well.
runners.comment: Back to form when third last week and now has something to build on; interesting

runners.name: Rhythm N Hooves
runners.spotlight: Won at Royal Ascot in 2023 and second in this race in 2025; the handicapper has been in command for much of 2026 but he went close at Windsor last month; not in the same form at Newmarket two weeks ago but the switch from cheekpieces to a visor could help; contender.
runners.comment: Conditions to suit & 5lb lower than when 2nd in this race in 2025; new headgear tried now

runners.name: Pilgrim
runners.spotlight: Enjoyed his finest hour when winning the Palace Of Holyrood House Stakes at the Royal meeting in 2024; gained his first win since when narrowly landing a 5f handicap at Musselburgh in April; two solid efforts have followed and he would appear likely to make another bold bid.
runners.comment: Royal Ascot winner in 2024; running well this year and should be in the thick of it again

runners.name: Underwriter
runners.spotlight: Won twice at Ayr (6f) in novice/maiden company last term either side of a heavy defeat in the Coventry Stakes; has struggled so far this year, including when 100-1 for his stable debut 15 days ago.
runners.comment: Yet to offer much this year and he needs to leave his recent stable debut well behind him

runners.name: Kylian
runners.spotlight: Patchy record for his new stable this year but he has run well over C&D in the past and has dropped to a tempting mark; cheekpieces replace blinkers today; couldn't discount.
runners.comment: On a tempting mark and has run well over C&D in the past; prominent showing expected
runners.owner: Middleham Park Racing Xii & Mrs G Cowell

runners.name: Almaty Star
runners.spotlight: Front-runner who was beaten off only inside the final 1f at Lingfield last time; should make another bold bid but he's still 4lb higher than when making all at Yarmouth in the spring.
runners.comment: Front-runner; in form but still 4lb higher than when making all at Yarmouth in the spring

runners.name: Cayman Tai
runners.spotlight: In good form in the spring, winning over this trip at Southwell, but his two most recent runs have been some way below par; others preferred.
runners.comment: In good form in the spring but two most recent runs have been below par; others preferred

runners.name: Mon Na Slieve
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer; on a lenient mark but his losing sequence is mounting and he had no obvious excuses when beating just one home at Beverley three weeks ago.
runners.comment: Losing sequence is mounting and no obvious excuses at Beverley three weeks ago

runners.name: Emerald Harmony
runners.spotlight: Tough cookie who arrives in peak form after a close third over C&D two weeks ago; one of three with serious claims for her local yard.
runners.comment: Tough cookie who arrives in peak form after close third over C&D two weeks ago

runners.name: Tees Aggregates
runners.spotlight: June win came in a small field at Catterick (5f) but he finished behind Kodiac Thriller when only seventh of nine at Ripon next time; well beaten on only run at York; bit to prove.
runners.comment: June win came in small field at Catterick; only seventh of nine at Ripon next time
runners.owner: Ingleby Bloodstock Ltd & The Ivy League

runners.name: Sports Coach
runners.spotlight: Had slipped in the weights before returning to form when second of 12 at Newcastle last month, coming close to landing a gamble; still 4lb below his last winning mark and should be in the mix again.
runners.comment: Came close to landing a gamble at Newcastle last time; should be in the mix again

runners.name: Ventura Express
runners.spotlight: Seems to be going through the motions and his losing run stretches back over two years; needs to stop the slide but he's on a dangerous mark if staging a revival, so impossible to rule out.
runners.comment: Losing run stretches back over two years but on a dangerous mark if staging a revival

runners.name: Cameley Days
runners.spotlight: 3-11 on turf; steadily progressive but most recent success came off 11lb lower and she'll need another personal best to notch win number four.
runners.comment: Steadily progressive but will need another personal best to notch win number four

runners.name: Bayraat
runners.spotlight: Plucky veteran who retains plenty of vim and vigour, another fine run when second in amateurs' race at Doncaster last time; 3lb out of the weights but has finished third in the last two runnings of this event and has each-way possibilities once more.
runners.comment: Plucky veteran; third in last two runnings and has each-way possibilities once more

runners.name: Managing Director
runners.spotlight: Has had far less racing than most of these and showed he retains ability when fifth of eight at Beverley (5f, good to firm; 11-1) three weeks ago after a long absence, a gelding operation and a stable switch; big player if coming on for that run and Danny McMenamin was the successful rider in this race last year, for the same connections.
runners.comment: Lightly raced; pleasing fifth at Beverley after layoff; big player if building on that

runners.name: Dream Deal
runners.spotlight: Winning for the fourth time when scoring at Beverley in June, and he was narrowly beaten in a blanket finish there on Monday; not ruled out.
runners.comment: Four-time winner; narrowly beaten in a blanket finish on Monday; not ruled out

runners.name: Roberto Caro
runners.spotlight: 4lb lower than for his last two 6f wins but recent efforts have been underwhelming and he's unproven over the minimum trip.
runners.comment: Recent efforts have been underwhelming and he's unproven at 5f

runners.name: Harb
runners.spotlight: Two 5f wins in 2026 and he ran respectably when third at Hamilton two weeks ago; prone to the odd poor run, however, and others are higher up the list.
runners.comment: Two 5f wins in 2026 but others are higher up the list

runners.name: Vince L'Amour
runners.spotlight: C&D winner earlier in career and also won off today's mark at Ripon in May, but he's been tailed off on his last two outings and urgently needs a reversal of fortune.
runners.comment: C&D winner; tailed off last two outings and urgently needs a reversal of fortune

runners.name: Kodiac Thriller
runners.spotlight: Returned to form when fourth in first-time visor at Ripon (5f, good) three weeks ago despite stumbling and nearly losing his rider at the start; possibilities off same mark if the headgear has the same effect.
runners.comment: Back to form in first-time visor at Ripon; possibilities off the same mark

runners.name: Lethal Nymph
runners.spotlight: Probably best at 5f and went down by only a head at Pontefract five weeks ago; had previously shaped well when fifth in a big field on this course; trainer has won this race three times in the last eight seasons and Johnny Burke looks a positive jockey booking.
runners.comment: Beaten only a head at Pontefract five weeks ago; trainer has a fine record in this race

runners.name: King's Call
runners.spotlight: Hard to fancy on recent efforts with no better than a tenth-placed finish in his last five starts; however, he could be revived by a recent stable switch (from Seb Spencer) and he's fully 18lb lower than when eighth in the 5f handicap at Royal Ascot last summer; worth monitoring in the market.
runners.comment: Hard to fancy on recent efforts but well handicapped and could be revived by stable switch

runners.name: Havana Rum
runners.spotlight: Stayed on from well off the pace to take third in a 0-80 over C&D a fortnight ago; this is tougher but likely to give another good account.
runners.comment: Good third over C&D two weeks ago; up in class but likely to give a good account

runners.name: Air Force One
runners.spotlight: 5f win on this card last year and he followed it was a hugely eye-catching third over 5.4f at the Ebor meeting; back in the winners' enclosure at Beverley in April and he has run well in defeat here and at Newcastle on his last two starts; can fluff the start and he still has to prove himself at 6f but there is an air of unfinished business surrounding him.
runners.comment: Has to prove himself at 6f but looks the type with more to offer; won on this card in 2025

runners.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners.spotlight: Beat 17 rivals at Thirsk in April and he has finished second three times since, including a big-field C&D handicap; missed out by a short-head at Newmarket last week; solid form claims despite small rise in the weights.
runners.comment: Enjoying a good summer for his new stable, including C&D; should remain competitive

runners.name: Musical Touch
runners.spotlight: The winner of two of his three starts in 2026, notably a big-field Class 4 over C&D six weeks ago; 4lb higher in a stronger race and his draw may not be advantageous.
runners.comment: 2-3 this year, including a big-field C&D handicapper; up in class and high draw a query

runners.name: Evening Blues
runners.spotlight: Promising at up to 1m for Ger Lyons as a 2yo; unplaced in his first two runs (7f/1m1f) for this yard but he turned in a career-best effort when second of 14 (behind a handicap blot; pair clear) over C&D four weeks ago; showed good speed on that occasion and he should make a bold bid from stall 1 despite a 4lb rise.
runners.comment: Drop to 6f worked the oracle when 2nd of 14 behind a handicap blot here latest; big player

runners.name: Rock Opera
runners.spotlight: Run of in-frame efforts came to an end here two weeks ago but he still ran with more promise than his finishing position suggests; still likely vulnerable at this level.
runners.comment: Better than the bare result here two weeks ago but probably vulnerable at this level

runners.name: Novello Lad
runners.spotlight: Progressive sprinter in 2025 (following wind surgery) and he has carried on the good work this year, winning 6f handicaps at Doncaster in May (good to soft) and June (good to firm); well beaten at Thirsk 24 days ago, however, and this is a deeper race.
runners.comment: Came up shy in hat-trick bid at Thirsk 24 days ago; this looks even tougher

runners.name: Stratusnine
runners.spotlight: Just one win to his name since returning to action in November and that is scant reward for some fine efforts, including an unlucky defeat over 5f here in May; good third at Chester (6f, good; drawn wide) four weeks ago; remains a sprinter of interest.
runners.comment: Not had much luck this year and he remains a sprinter of interest

runners.name: Red Spells Danger
runners.spotlight: His form has taken off since dropped to 6f, winning at Ripon and Hamilton in May and posting fine efforts in defeat over C&D and at Newmarket since; no obvious reason why he wouldn't be in the shake up again.
runners.comment: Made good progress since dropped to 6f, including here; still not fully exposed

runners.name: Addison Grey
runners.spotlight: Began the year with two good efforts at Newbury and Newmarket; beaten favourite on his last two starts but that is not to say this mark will prove beyond him if things pan out more favourably; each-way shout if a high draw doesn't prove to be a negative.
runners.comment: String of good runs in defeat this year; should be suited by the demands of this race

runners.name: Pocklington
runners.spotlight: Rated 5lb higher than when a close fifth in this race 12 months ago; has done well on AW since, winning at Southwell (well backed) on New Year's Day and finishing a good fourth at Newcastle four weeks ago; not obviously thrown in but could still have a bit more to come.
runners.comment: Not far off best when 4th at Newcastle latest; has C&D form; respected despite topweight

runners.name: Veblen Good
runners.spotlight: Made a winning stable debut at Pontefract (6f, good to firm) in April; two good 6f runs this month too but he will need to pull out more if he is to come out on top this afternoon.
runners.comment: Good efforts in defeat twice this month but he will need more to come out on top here

runners.name: We Never Stop
runners.spotlight: Three poor runs to begin his turf campaign but he underwent wind surgery in June and returned to form with a close second at Chester (6f, good) four weeks ago; not certain to confirm those placings with Stratusnine.
runners.comment: Had a wind op in June and returned with a good second at Chester; this is tougher

runners.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners.spotlight: Won last season's Portland handicap at Doncaster off a 1lb higher mark; she made a slow start to 2026 but there have been encouraging signs more recently, fourth at Ayr (6f, soft) and then second at Doncaster (5f, good to firm); form dipped here (5f, good to firm) two weeks ago; could bounce back.
runners.comment: On good mark on last year's best; trending in right direction until lesser run here latest

runners.name: Trilby
runners.spotlight: He has run well over C&D in the past and he arrives in fine form, winning 5f handicaps at Haydock and Carlisle (soft/good to soft) this summer; the 5lb rise is less of a concern than either his draw in stall 22 or the forecast faster ground.
runners.comment: Arrives in top form but draw/ground concerns this time

runners.name: Rousing Encore
runners.spotlight: Won a good C&D handicap last year and also successful at Ayr last September; 0-7 in 2026 but he retains all his ability and ran well for third (of 17) at Ayr 19 days ago; high draw a potential stumbling block.
runners.comment: C&D winner on fast ground last May; 0-7 in 2026 but retains all his ability; draw a query

runners.name: Coul Angel
runners.spotlight: Made good progress in the second half of 2025; the handicapper has held the upper hand more recently though and this might not set up ideally for his style of racing.
runners.comment: Progressive last year; the handicapper has been in command this time around though

runners.name: Baldomero
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 in fine form on AW; 0-7 in 2026 but he has slipped 6lb below his last winning mark and has Toby Moore taking another 7lb off his back; suspicion a few will prove stronger.
runners.comment: Ended 2025 in fine form on AW; this year has been more challenging; others look stronger

runners.name: Utmost Respect
runners.spotlight: Promising in his first three 2yo runs but he couldn't quite cut the mustard in nurseries thereafter; gelded prior to his reappearance; still has time to do better but he returns in a warm race.
runners.comment: Came up short in nurseries in the second half of 2025; been gelded; returns in a good race

runners.name: Apollo One
runners.spotlight: Admirable campaigner down the years and although he hasn't placed in three visits to York, he has been poorly drawn in two of them and ran well in Listed company on the other occasion; looked to retain ability when third at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) on 2000 Guineas day and he shouldn't be crabbed for his Wokingham effort as he trounced the only other rival to race up the stands' rail; it has been a long time since he's had a mark this low; big run on the cards.
runners.comment: Veteran but on a good mark and in better form than his numbers suggest; big run expected

runners.name: Commanche Falls
runners.spotlight: Veteran who ran a cracker behind a stablemate over C&D at last season's Ebor meeting; runner-up twice in Bahrain in January; low-key return to Britain last week; on a good mark but this is a tough race in which to try and rebound.
runners.comment: Conditions suit and on good mark but this veteran needs to leave last week's return behind
runners.owner: Doug Graham, Ian Davison, Alan Drysdale

runners.name: Damysus
runners.spotlight: Second to Pride Of Arras in last year's Dante over C&D; looked set for a stellar 2026 when trouncing five rivals in Group 3 at Newmarket (1m1f, good) on reappearance, but hasn't repeated the form in 1m Group 1s since; stepping back up in distance looks a sensible move and he's the one to beat judged on that standout Newmarket effort.
runners.comment: Not at best in 1m Group 1s but Newmarket 1m1f Group 3 rout gives him serious claims

runners.name: Item
runners.spotlight: Beat subsequent Derby winner Christmas Day in the Group 2 Dante over C&D (good ground) in May, only to finish well beaten behind that rival on much softer ground at Epsom (11-2); still low-mileage and looked potentially top-class in the Dante; may get back on track on today's forecast firmer ground.
runners.comment: Impressive in Dante before well beaten in soft-ground Derby; may get back on track

runners.name: Royal Champion
runners.spotlight: Nine wins in a varied career include this race 12 months ago and a Group 1 in Saudi Arabia (10.5f, good to firm) in February; far from disgraced in Hong Kong last time and now returns from three months off; should give his running but a 5lb penalty makes the task more difficult.
runners.comment: Last year's winner; should give his running but 5lb penalty makes the task more difficult
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

runners.name: Dancing Gemini
runners.spotlight: Most recent success came in Group 2 at Sandown (1m, good) last April; not at best in three runs this season, including in same race and when returned to 1m2f for Group 1 at Royal Ascot five weeks ago; needs a revival.
runners.comment: Group 2 winner last term but not at best in three runs this season and needs a revival

runners.name: Pride Of Arras
runners.spotlight: Has an unblemished record at York, winning the Dante (1m2f) and Great Voltigeur (1m4f) last season; had a delayed start to 2026 due to a bruised foot and almost certainly needed the run when last of eight in the Group 1 Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud three weeks ago; interesting with that outing behind him and back on the Knavesmire.
runners.comment: Probably needed reappearance in French Group 1; interesting back at York (2-2 in Group 2s)

races.race_name: Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap

runners.name: Son
runners.spotlight: Campaigned solely at 7f this term but shapes as if he'll be well suited by this return to 1m; has met trouble in running on his last two starts; thrown in on the pick of his form for Richard Hannon and could be ready to strike.
runners.comment: Short of room on his last two starts; thrown in on his best form; could be ready to strike

runners.name: Canvas
runners.spotlight: Front-runner with a favourable low draw; shaped nicely at Newmarket (1m, good) on reappearance and quick ground was blamed for a poor run next time; below the mark of his last win (over C&D) and no surprise if he makes a bold bid from the front, especially if the rain materialises.
runners.comment: Shaped nicely on return and had an excuse last time; could make a bold bid from the front

runners.name: Madame De Sevigne
runners.spotlight: Far more miss than hit this season and beat only one home at Newmarket last time; others preferred.
runners.comment: Far more miss than hit this season and beat only one home at Newmarket last time

runners.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners.spotlight: Nosed home at Redcar (1m, good) in May and ran creditably when a close third at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) two weeks ago; her mark is unchanged but she's up from a 0-65 to a 0-80.
runners.comment: Close third at Doncaster two weeks ago; mark unchanged but she is up in grade

runners.name: Cancan In The Rain
runners.spotlight: Won two from five last season and looks as good as ever this term, fourth in a big field at Ascot two weeks ago; effective at 7f and 1m; should be in the thick of things again.
runners.comment: Looks as good as ever this term, fourth at Ascot two weeks ago; in the mix again

runners.name: Rajapour
runners.spotlight: Had been bubbling under prior to winning easily at Redcar (1m, good to firm) on Sunday, and given the style of that success he looks an attractive proposition under a 5lb penalty; high on the list.
runners.comment: Easy winner at Redcar on Sunday; attractive proposition under 5lb penalty

runners.name: Dwindling Funds
runners.spotlight: Consistent type who won six times last season and arrives on the back of two close seconds; this race looks deeper than his last two but he's in fine form and unlikely to be far away.
runners.comment: Close second last two starts; this race looks deeper but he's unlikely to be far away
runners.owner: D P Van Der Hoeven & D G Pryde

runners.name: Up The Jazz
runners.spotlight: Arrives on a recent high after a win at Musselburgh and a second at Ripon (both 1m, good); should give his running but he's up in grade here.
runners.comment: Arrives on recent high after win at Musselburgh and second at Ripon; up in grade here

runners.name: Paladin
runners.spotlight: Sprang a 33-1 surprise on stable debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in January, and back to form when second at Ascot (1m, good to firm) two weeks ago; should be thereabouts.
runners.comment: Back to form when second at Ascot two weeks ago; should be thereabouts

runners.name: Final Night
runners.spotlight: All four wins on the AW but he's just as effective on turf; needs to bounce back from a poor run at Newmarket's July meeting but he's down sharply in grade here and his form from the spring has a solid look to it.
runners.comment: Below par last time but down sharply in grade here and spring form has a solid look to it

runners.name: Draupnir
runners.spotlight: Upped markedly in trip here (1m6f) four weeks ago and predictably failed to stay; previous form (7f-1m1f) is solid enough but a wide draw could be difficult to overcome.
runners.comment: Failed to stay 1m6f last time; previous form solid enough but today's wide draw is tricky

runners.name: Montezin
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; hasn't had the rub of the green of late, repeatedly denied a run when stepped up to 1m at Newcastle four weeks ago; respected.
runners.comment: Lightly raced 4yo; hasn't had the rub of the green of late; respected

runners.name: Barley
runners.spotlight: Just three wins but has been second or third 17 times, including on his last four starts; stall 17 could be tricky.
runners.comment: Just three wins but has been second or third 17 times; wide draw not ideal

runners.name: Enola Grey
runners.spotlight: Has a better strike-rate on AW than grass but she's in better form than her last two turf runs suggest, short of room at Ascot on latest; less obvious than several of these but not ruled out.
runners.comment: In better form than her last two runs suggest; less obvious than some but not ruled out

runners.name: Financer
runners.spotlight: Had slipped in the weights before winning at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) on Sunday; not certain to be as effective back at 1m and he's ridden by an apprentice with a smaller claim.
runners.comment: Redcar winner on Sunday; down in trip here and ridden by apprentice with smaller claim
runners.owner: S Bulmer, P Hebdon & R Taylor

runners.name: Bowood
runners.spotlight: Falling in the weights and ran respectably when third to Rajapour at Redcar on Sunday, but the winner bolted up that day and it's hard to see the tables being turned.
runners.comment: Third to Rajapour at Redcar but the winner bolted up; hard to see the tables being turned

races.race_name: Sky Bet Price Boosts EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners.name: Bear Lee
runners.spotlight: Overcame slow start to win comfortably at Musselburgh (5f, good) last month; open to further progress and should be just as effective back at 6f, but carries a penalty in what looks a stronger race.
runners.comment: Comfortable Musselburgh winner; unexposed, but penalised in what looks a stronger race
runners.owner: N Bradley Racing 29, D Scott & P Spencer

runners.name: Desert Smoke
runners.spotlight: Did her best work late on after a slow start when sixth at Newmarket (6f, good to firm; 17-2) two weeks ago, finishing a place behind Hout Bay; like that rival, she could make quite a bit of progress for the experience.
runners.comment: Best work late on when sixth on debut at Newmarket; could make quite a bit of progress

runners.name: Hout Bay
runners.spotlight: 150,000euros breeze-up buy; went off 50-1 but shaped nicely when fifth of 11 at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) two weeks ago, rallying after being short of room; could improve significantly and commands major respect.
runners.comment: Met trouble when encouraging fifth at Newmarket on debut and could improve significantly
runners.owner: J Sarkar, D Sarkar, O Sarkar & D Sarkar

runners.name: Gladys Pugh
runners.spotlight: 200,000gns yearling; too green to do herself justice (slowly away, flashed tail soon after start) when fifth on debut over C&D (6-1) earlier this month; plenty of improvement required but she might have learned a lot.
runners.comment: Very green when fifth on debut over C&D; improvement required but might have learned a lot
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid

runners.name: Nour
runners.spotlight: Seemed to know her job and shaped encouragingly when 1l third of nine at Redcar (6f, good to firm; 5-2) in May, always up with the pace; that form is probably nothing special but she's in good hands and should progress.
runners.comment: Third of nine at Redcar in May, always up with the pace; in good hands and should progress

runners.name: Rogue Jewel
runners.spotlight: £50,000 yearling, £75,000 breeze-up 2yo; by Mehmas; dam Group-placed 7f/1m winner (including 2yo; RPR 108), out of US 8.5f Grade 2 winner; upwardly mobile stable had its first 2yo winner of the season earlier this month; well worth a market check.
runners.comment: Upwardly mobile yard had first 2yo winner of season two weeks ago; worth a market check

races.race_name: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners.name: Humble Spark
runners.spotlight: On a long losing run and never a threat here two weeks ago, but he'd previously been beaten just a nose in the Queen Mother's Cup over C&D in June; none too reliable but a danger to all if he's on a going day.
runners.comment: Beaten a nose here in June; none too reliable but a danger to all if he's on a going day

runners.name: Damascus Steel
runners.spotlight: Represents a new trainer in excellent form and has won at Goodwood (1m4f, good) and Epsom (1m4f, good to firm) on his last two outings, proving himself better than ever; edging up the weights only gradually and in the mix again.
runners.comment: Better than ever with Goodwood and Epsom wins; does just enough and in the mix again

runners.name: Caliban
runners.spotlight: Arrives on a hat-trick after 1m3f AW wins for Andrew Balding at Kempton and Southwell, after which he was sold for 50,000gns; not fully proven on turf, although he did show promise at Haydock on his debut; has joined a very capable stable and may not have reached his ceiling just yet.
runners.comment: Arrives on hat-trick after AW wins for Andrew Balding; may not have reached ceiling yet

runners.name: Tycoon
runners.spotlight: Could be unexposed at 1m4f and ran creditably on first attempt at trip when third of eight at Ascot (good to firm) two weeks ago; goes well for positive tactics and Toby Moore's 7lb claim is a bonus.
runners.comment: Front-runner; unexposed at 1m4f; third at Ascot last time; rider's 7lb claim is a bonus

runners.name: The Glen Rovers
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 7yo; has an impressive strike-rate but all six of his wins have come on the AW and he hasn't been placed in four runs on turf; below par last time and has a fair bit to prove.
runners.comment: All six wins have come on the AW; fair bit to prove on turf

runners.name: Likealot
runners.spotlight: Bred to be useful and has been steadily progressive; clearcut winner at Lingfield (1m4f) towards end of 2025 and shaped well over inadequate 1m2f at Chester (good) on reappearance; this step back up in distance should be perfect and she has rock-solid claims.
runners.comment: Shaped well over inadequate 1m2f on reappearance and this step back up in trip is ideal

runners.name: Ashnak
runners.spotlight: Hasn't been long with David O'Meara and he looks to be building up to something, bumping in to an improver when second of 12 at Ayr (1m5f, soft) five weeks ago; quick ground would be an unknown but otherwise he has plenty in his favour.
runners.comment: Unexposed for this yard; second to an improver at Ayr last time; has plenty in his favour

runners.name: Chillingham
runners.spotlight: Awarded C&D Queen Mother's Cup last June and much lower in the weights now, but that's because his form has fallen off a cliff; dangerous if blinkers (replacing other headgear) spark a revival but carries clear risks.
runners.comment: Thrown in on best form but has lost his way completely; blinkers replace other headgear

runners.name: Therapist
runners.spotlight: Formerly trained by Andrew Balding and Nicky Henderson; sole Flat win came over 1m2f in 2023 but she has since won five times over hurdles; ran creditably over 2m at Lingfield at the start of the year before being sold for £6,000 in May; worth a check in the market.
runners.comment: One Flat win and five over hurdles for previous yards; sold relatively cheaply in May

runners.name: Wahdan
runners.spotlight: Useful 3yo when based in France, largely disappointing for Joseph O'Brien last year; some promise for current yard, not helped by racing wide at Chester (1m2f) last time; moves into unknown territory trip-wise but his mark is falling and he's impossible to discount.
runners.comment: Trip an unknown but he's well treated on his best form and had an excuse last time

runners.name: Return Of The Gods
runners.spotlight: Bar a blip on AW in the spring (wore a first-time tongue tie which was quickly discarded) his profile is steadily progressive, edging out Alpha Capture (due to run here on Friday) in 7f Doncaster handicap (good to firm) 16 days ago; 4lb higher now back in a 3yo only race but he may have more to give.
runners.comment: Largely progressive, shading tight finish in 7f Doncaster handicap latest; up 4lb

runners.name: Toastmaster
runners.spotlight: Struck at the third time of asking for Micheal Herrington when seeing off Flight Control and 11 others in handicap at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month; Flight Control finished a couple of places ahead of him at the Newmarket July meeting since but it was another sound effort from this son of Cotai Glory.
runners.comment: Beat Flight Control when off mark in June; behind that rival when fair fifth since; claims
runners.owner: Follow The Majer Partners & S Herrington

runners.name: Milford Grange
runners.spotlight: Shaped well when runner-up on three successive starts (6f/7f, good to soft/soft) but never better than midfield when faced with a firmer surface over 1m here 15 days ago; quickly drops back in trip with a visor also added.
runners.comment: Only midfield over 1m here latest but claims on form over shorter before that; visor added

runners.name: Flight Control
runners.spotlight: Promising start to handicap career, chasing home Toastmaster at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) before finishing a couple of places ahead of that rival when third of 11 at Newmarket (7f, good to firm again) a fortnight ago; handily drawn and should go well again.
runners.comment: Promising start to handicap career (closely matched with Toastmaster); should go well

runners.name: Invincible Boy
runners.spotlight: Scored with authority on his return in Pontefract novice (6f, good to soft) in April; never on the pace when well-beaten eighth of 14 in 6f handicap here 12 weeks later but it's possible he'll benefit from this step up to 7f and remains unexposed after four starts; going than firmer than good would be a first.
runners.comment: 6f novice win on return but never going pace in 6f handicap here since; 7f may help

runners.name: Gunalt Wavelength
runners.spotlight: Beaten on first ten starts but got off the mark at the 11th attempt at Ripon (6f, good) in May and followed up in big field at Doncaster (7f, good); his winning run was ended back at Doncaster but ran with credit again in fourth.
runners.comment: Back-to-back wins at the start of the summer but found out off this mark last time

runners.name: Bright Summer
runners.spotlight: Built upon the promise of her debut fourth at Newbury (7f, good) in April when winning maiden at Lingfield (7f, AW) in May; well beaten on soft ground at Salisbury next time but bounced back with a respectable sixth on Chester handicap debut four weeks ago; that was a 0-95 so this represents a slight drop in grade; remains lightly raced for a leading yard.
runners.comment: AW maiden winner; fair start to handicap career in Chester 0-95 since

runners.name: Dacres Cross
runners.spotlight: Won a Carlisle nursery (6f, good) last August; best run since when fourth of 20 over C&D (good) but failed to build on it when fifth of nine at Catterick 17 days ago.
runners.comment: Good fourth of 20 over C&D in May but failed to build on it at Catterick 17 days ago

runners.name: Mr Noble
runners.spotlight: Sent off 5-4 when beating six rivals on his debut at Newcastle (6f) in December; hasn't advanced his form in two subsequent outings but it was a sound start to his handicap career when third of 14 in 6f course handicap (good) latterly; stuck on after getting outpaced in a style which suggests this extra 1f will suit; has to enter the reckoning.
runners.comment: Good start to handicap career when third over 14 over 6f here and 7f promises to suit

runners.name: Bleep Test
runners.spotlight: Of interest on her 2yo best but beaten a long way on both 6f starts this year; the combination of a step up in trip and addition of a tongue-tie needs to spark a big upturn in his fortunes.
runners.comment: Hard to fancy on her two 6f runs this year; goes up in trip with tongue-tie added

runners.name: Zarvali
runners.spotlight: Ex Irish-trained gelding who improved to make a winning start for Roger Fell in 7f Catterick novice in May; shaped quite well in handicaps over this trip on next two starts but in trouble before stamina should have been an issue when stepped up to 1m here since.
runners.comment: Run of good form for this yard ended when seventh over 1m here latest; quickly back at 7f

runners.name: Forest Phoenix
runners.spotlight: Got up late to win a 5f Catterick novice (good to firm) in May but beaten upwards of 10l in his five other starts, including course handicaps over 5f and 1m the last twice.
runners.comment: His 5f Catterick novice win in May is very much a standout so far

runners.name: Thankfully
runners.spotlight: Narrow winner of a Beverley maiden in April; matched that when fifth on her handicap debut at Thirsk (1m, good) but two lesser runs have followed; Mr Noble is the more obvious of the Karl Burke pair.
runners.comment: Hasn't built on Beverley maiden win in handicaps; Mr Noble more obvious of stable pair
runners.owner: Mrs Tabor, Mrs Mv Magnier, Mrs Shanahan

runners.name: Raging Raj
runners.spotlight: Ended time for Jane Chapple-Hyam by making all in 7f Yarmouth handicap (good to firm) four weeks ago; changed hands for 30,000gns since; new stable, which continues in good form, also runs Toastmaster; drawn wider than ideal.
runners.comment: Won at Yarmouth on final run for Jane Chapple-Hyam; new yard also runs Toastmaster

runners.name: Seaxburh
runners.spotlight: Showed the benefit of two Roscommon outings when producing an improved display in a 7f maiden at Down Royal eight days ago; finished in front of a shorter-priced stablemate in chasing home the front-running favourite (trained by Aidan O'Brien); cheekpieces may help; sets a fair standard.
runners.comment: Will not need to improve much from her Down Royal second to win here, cheekpieces may help

runners.name: Why Oh Why
runners.spotlight: E8,000 yearling; sixth foal; half-sister to a bumper winner; useful winning dam, half-sister by Holy Roman Emperor to 7f 2yo Group 3 winner Stonemason, out of sister to Jersey Stakes winner River Deep; from a recently-established local stable.
runners.comment: Half-sister to a bumper winner, dam a winning half-sister to 7f Group 3 winner Stonemason

runners.name: Old Joanie
runners.spotlight: Not a bad run at a huge price on debut at the Curragh; also some merit in last week's Leopardstown run; not a likely maiden winner, but could be interesting in a nursery after this.
runners.comment: Not disgraced in two maidens, could be interesting in a nursery after this

runners.name: Ana Morello
runners.spotlight: E15,000 yearling, first foal; dam AW winner, sister to 2yo Group 3 winner/1m Group 1-placed Marie's Diamond, half-sister to Australian 1m2f Listed winner Sikandarabad.
runners.comment: Dam AW winner, sister to 2yo Group 3 winner/1m Group 1-placed Marie's Diamond

runners.name: Sonic Sabiha
runners.spotlight: E20,000 yearling; fifth foal; half-sister to winners in the US and Slovakia; dam unraced half-sister to 1m4f Group 2 winner Strathspey.
runners.comment: Half-sister to two winners, dam an unraced half-sister to 1m4f Group 2 winner Strathspey

runners.name: Spectrolyte
runners.spotlight: E42,000 yearling; State Of Rest filly is a half-sister to 6f AW 2yo winner Karaoke; dam US 6.5f dirt winner, half-sister to Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf winner Hootenanny; stable set to have best season, but yet to have a juvenile winner this term.
runners.comment: State Of Rest filly, half-sister to 6f AW winner; dam a well-related US 6.5f dirt winner

runners.name: Diamonds And Dames
runners.spotlight: E55,000 yearling; eighth foal; half-sister by Churchill to five winners, best of them Sixteen Arches (American Grade 2-placed); dam unraced half-sister to 5f 2yo Group 3 winner Tournedos;
runners.comment: Half-sister by Churchill to five winners, best of them US Grade 2-placed, could feature

runners.name: Matavai Bay
runners.spotlight: E40,000 yearling; third foal; half-sister by Dandy Man to two winners; dam German Listed-placed 6f winner, half-sister to a German 1m1f Listed winner.
runners.comment: E40,000 yearling, third foal; half-sister to two winners, dam German Listed-placed winner

runners.name: Sword Of State
runners.spotlight: Half-sister by State Of Rest to five winners, best of them a 7f Listed scorer; not beaten far in a decent maiden at the Curragh last Sunday; could run into the money now with that experience under her belt.
runners.comment: Not beaten far in a decent maiden at the Curragh last Sunday, could run into the money now

runners.name: Thelymitra
runners.spotlight: Never in the hunt first time out at Leopardstown; stable's second-string then, same scenario now.
runners.comment: Never in the hunt first time out at Leopardstown, stable's second-string as  she was then

runners.name: Liamo
runners.spotlight: Sole win from 22 starts came at Listowel last summer (off 40); fair sixth at the same venue in May on seasonal debut; perhaps unlucky not to finish closer when 5l sixth of 13 at Killarney ten days ago, had to be wait to get a clear run.
runners.comment: Perhaps unlucky not to finish closer when sixth at Killarney ten days ago, may do better

runners.name: Roman Harry
runners.spotlight: Laytown winner in 2024 and won a 7f claimer at Dundalk last December; some fair runs in 7f/1m Dundalk handicaps in the spring; 0-28 record on turf is a significant negative.
runners.comment: Best form on AW (also a Laytown winner), 0-28 record on turf is a significant negative.

runners.name: Will Be King
runners.spotlight: Almost three years since he last ran on turf and has a better overall record on AW; missed 2024 and 2025; pleasing reappearance at Wolverhampton in March; doubts raised by subsequent form; new headgear combination now.
runners.comment: Almost three years since he last ran on turf and has a better overall record on AW

runners.name: Baby Basma
runners.spotlight: Won an early-season 5f Cork maiden last year; did not appear again until March this year; two ordinary Dundalk runs in the spring; has a bit to find with Princess Chloe and Dawn Flame on running at Limerick a fortnight ago.
runners.comment: 5f winner at two, a bit to find with Princess Chloe and Dawn Flame on Limerick running

runners.name: Variance
runners.spotlight: Has looked very limited; 50-1 when finishing in rear over 1m at Bellewstown on handicap/seasonal debut at Bellewstown.
runners.comment: Has looked very limited, 50-1 when finishing in rear over 1m on handicap/seasonal debut

runners.name: Hero Of The Hour
runners.spotlight: Seven wins between turf and AW over 5f-6f for his previous trainers; made a bright start for this stable when fourth over 6f at Fairyhouse last month; mid-division in two more recent outings.
runners.comment: Seven wins for his previous trainers, has failed to build on a promising stable debut

runners.name: Mini Cotai
runners.spotlight: Best run this season was over 5f on soft ground when second from out of the handicap at Down Royal; has done plenty of racing lately and has become unreliable.
runners.comment: Best run this year was over 5f on soft, has done plenty of racing lately, unreliable

runners.name: Princess Chloe
runners.spotlight: First four runs were at Dundalk; fair fourth of 13 at 200-1 in a 7f maiden in February; never a threat in a handicap later that month; made a promising start to her turf career when second over 7f at Limerick two weeks ago; not much to choose between her and Dawn Flame who met trouble in running
runners.comment: Made a promising start to her turf career when second  at Limerick, Dawn Flame third then

runners.name: Romantic War
runners.spotlight: Placed in a couple of 7f/1m handicaps last October on soft/heavy off basement mark; labouring this season and impossible to fancy on recent showings; last of nine in a claimer at Ballinrobe on Monday.
runners.comment: Placed on soft/heavy last October,  labouring this season, impossible to fancy

runners.name: Maker's Mark
runners.spotlight: Has been running over longer trips; improved slightly on moderate form when fifth at Down Royal last month; had only one behind in a 1m3f Naas contest last time.
runners.comment: Has been running over longer trips, had only one behind in a 1m3f Naas contest last time
runners.owner: Hugh J O'Brien & Colm O'Brien & Ms Denise McCourt

runners.name: Dawn Flame
